newsitem.title: INDIA: B.A.T official questioned in ITC case.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T official questioned in ITC case.

text.p: Indian authorities began questioning an executive of Britain's B.A.T Industries Plc on Thursday in connection with a probe into alleged foreign exchange violations by its Indian associate ITC Ltd, officials said.
Richard Pilbeam, who until recently served as a B.A.T nominee on ITC's board of directors, arrived at the Enforcement Directorate's Calcutta office in the late morning, witnesses said.
He was taken to the office of the deputy director of the directorate's eastern region, K.K. Kabirpanthi, officials said.
"Yes, we have started questioning Mr Pilbeam," an Enforcement Directorate official told Reuters.
The British tobacco and financial services group is the single biggest shareholder in ITC with 31.7 percent.

Pilbeam was the second B.A.T official to be questioned by the investigating agency. On November 14, Malcolm Fry, managing director of VST Ltd and a former B.A.T nominee on the ITC board, was questioned by enforcement officials.
The case broke into public view last month when the Enforcement Directorate launched nationwide raids into homes and offices of ITC officials.
Among those arrested were two former ITC chairmen and several serving or retired senior executives.
The Enforcement Directorate is an arm of the Finance Ministry, which has said the violations involved up to $100 million in ITC's international operations.
On November 6, B.A.T said that its fundamental attitude towards India and ITC remained positive and one of continued commitment.
